newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures finish mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures finish mostly higher.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished mostly higher, with September marks and Swiss francs at one-week highs and yen lower.
With the Group of Seven summit over and Japan's quarterly "tankan" business report ahead, traders said the market was due to consolidate for now.
"Pretty quiet here is the expectation," said Ralph Delzenero, vice president of foreign exchange marketing for First Chicago.
He said foreign exchange activity tapered off once Europe closed, leaving most prices rangebound in the afternoon.
September yen futures found good buying late and closed near the day's peak, traders noted.
Analysts cited reported comments by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto that Japan might be tempted to sell U.S. Treasuries if needed to stabilize dollar/yen.

"It seems to be sending a signal to the market that there could be heightened tension between the U.S. and Japan," said Mike Malpede, Refco senior currency analyst. "It spooked the bonds and it spooked the dollar/yen."
The comment was reportedly made in a question-and-answer session following a speech at Columbia University.
Despite the late gains, September yen still closed lower.
September sterling rose to the highest price in a year and extended its rally late, fueled by technical momentum and ongoing expectations for higher rates.
One trader also called sterling a safe haven for European Monetary Union concerns in continental Europe.
"The marks and Swiss were relatively steady for the remainder of the day, though," the trader said. "I think it's going to be mostly range trading" before tankan, he said.
September mark and Swiss franc futures nudged to more than one-week highs but found scant followthrough.
Marks were held back initially by resistance at Friday's $0.5848 high before crawling above minor resistance at $0.5855. One currency analyst put resistance above there at $0.5860.
Swiss francs breached resistance at $0.7050 but stalled out below the next cap at $0.7070.

At the close, September yen was off $0.000025 at $0.008801, marks rose $0.0028 to $0.5852, Swiss francs rose $0.0038 to $0.7053, sterling was up $0.0158 at $1.6682, Canadian dollars were up $0.0021 at $0.7247, Australian dollars fell $0.0005 to $0.7519 and Mexican pesos were $0.000300 higher at $0.121450. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
